transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-09-29
Start: 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Liam (Redwood SE), Sofia (CSM), Dr. Arjun Mehta (NimbleHealth Eng Lead), Hannah (SRE), Carlos (Product), Mina (Dev)
Links shared: https://redwood.ai/pilot-results.xlsx, https://redwood.ai/reliability-deck.pdf, ticket# 12345

Summary: quick triage of last week's incident where we saw intermittent 5xx + client timeouts under a hotkey surge; focus on retry budgets, adaptive backoff, and KV prefix caching warmup. Agreement to test adjusted retry windows and run two synthetic spikes.

--- Transcript body (timestamps approximate) ---
[00:00] Maya: okay hey everyone thanks for hopping on, um this is our weekly P-O-C sync, i'm Maya from Redwood, and Liam's our SE today. quick roll call?
[00:07] Arjun: yep arjun here, hannah and carlos on my side, hey.
[00:10] Hannah: hi, yeah thanks.
[00:12] Liam: cool, I'll give a 5 minute recap of what we saw on friday and then we'll go into tuning. 
[00:20] Liam: so we saw a spike of roughly 3x qps for about 90 seconds, there was hotkey concentration around a subset of endpoints, our serving runtime started queuing and then some requests hit the global circuit breaker and surfaced 502/504-ish 5xx; couple of client-side timeouts as well.
[00:40] Mina: we've seen similar locally when a cron job flattens the cache, uh the K-V cash warm up is slow, sorry K-V cash — the KV cache.
[00:46] Liam: yeah that's right, the prefix cache wasn't warm so cold KV lookups added latency -> increased in-flight tokens -> queue growth -> circuit breaker.
[00:55] Carlos: curious about the exact 5xx patterns, were they more gateway errors or model OOMs?
[01:02] Liam: mostly gateway 5xx and some 502 from overloaded inference nodes; not an obvious OOM pattern. logs show worker queue length spike then a handful of RPC timeouts.
[01:15] Arjun: and we saw the client retry loop firing a bunch; our front-end tries 3 retries with small fixed backoff so it ended up amplifying the load.
[01:24] Hannah: yep, that made the tail worse.
[01:26] Maya: ok so two levers — server-side shedding/circuit break windowing and client retry backoff tuning. we recommended jittered exponential backoff and a retry budget.
[01:36] Liam: i'll put our suggested numbers: initial backoff 200ms, multiplier 2x, max backoff 2s, jitter 30%, and cap retries per logical request to 2 with a token-bucket retry budget shared across the user session. these are in the sheet.
[01:49] Arjun: 200ms seems low given our 150-200ms p95, wouldn't that still cause amplified traffic?
[01:55] Liam: good point — if your p95 baseline is 150ms then starting at 300ms may be safer, we can propose values tuned to your baseline.
[02:02] Maya: action: liam to add two parameter sets: conservative and aggressive.
[02:07] Liam: noted.
[02:10] Hannah: on the server side, would something like an adaptive concurrency limit help? we have kubernetes autoscale but the scale lag was noticeable.
[02:19] Liam: yes adaptive concurrency helps — Redwood's smart routing can also prefer cheaper model variants under pressure and auto-fallback; for the pilot we're recommending a soft shed: reject early on per-model long queue, incrementally route to smaller model variant rather than hard fail.
[02:33] Carlos: how disruptive is fallback to smaller models to accuracy? our product is sensitive to hallucinations so we want guardrails.
[02:40] Liam: you can set fidelity tiers: fallback only for requests flagged as non-core or for background async tasks; also add post-checks. plus we can do canary rollouts and compare quality metrics on the fly.
[02:54] Arjun: can we get an automated quality alert to avoid silent drops in output quality?
[02:58] Sofia: yes — Redwood Optimize has evaluation hooks and quality regressions tied to prompt sets; we can wire a webhook to your monitoring to open a ticket if quality dips >X%.
[03:08] Hannah: that'd be great.
[03:10] Maya: earlier you mentioned prefix cache warming. do you have warmup on deploy or do you rely on traffic?
[03:16] Mina: mostly traffic — we don't have a warmup job.
[03:19] Liam: okay, simplest fix is to run a pre-warm synthetic job post-deploy or keep a warm replica pool; also consider caching hot prefixes in a small in-memory store at edge to reduce cold reads to KV.
[03:31] Hannah: we can run a warmup job yes. is there a recommended pattern?
[03:35] Liam: we recommend generating realistic tokens distribution and hitting common hotkeys over 10 minutes. I'll share a script.
[03:40] Maya: we'll attach that script to the ticket.
[03:43] Arjun: about observability gaps — we saw missing span ids in some traces.
[03:47] Liam: yeah that's instrumentation drift — sometimes the SDK drops tracing headers on retries. we'll review the SDK integration snippet and send a patch.
[03:55] Hannah: ok.
[03:56] [04:00] Carlos: question on rate-limits — what's Redwood's rate-limit enforcement granularity? per-API-key, per-route, per-customer?
[04:07] Liam: by default per-api-key with per-route overrides; for Dedicated we can do per-customer pool. you can also configure token-level throttling.
[04:15] Carlos: we might want stricter per-route limits since the hotkey is one route.
[04:19] Liam: yep that's doable; we can add a targeted rule for that endpoint.
[04:23] Arjun: any changes to SLA if we add burst capacity?
[04:27] Maya: if you move to reserved burst we can guarantee more consistent latency but it affects price; i'll send an updated estimate.
[04:33] Mina: could you show the delta in per-token cost if we enable prefix cache + warmup?
[04:38] Maya: generally prefix caching reduces tokens by ~10-30% depending on reuse; i'll compute a scenario for your QPS and attach to the sheet.
[04:46] Hannah: on the incident timeline, can you walk us through the proposed mitigation sequence if a similar surge happens?
[04:50] Liam: yes — step 1: client slow-down (incremental backoff + retry budget), step 2: targeted per-route rate-limits + soft shed, step 3: enable fallback to smaller model variant for non-critical calls, step 4: if persistent, open capacity burst and autoscale up within SLA window, step 5: post-incident quality check.
[05:14] Arjun: sounds good.
[05:16] Maya: quick note — we saw one noisy neighbor effect in cloud region eu-west-1 last week, unrelated but worth flagging.
[05:22] Hannah: ok.
[05:23] Liam: for the test plan we propose: 1) apply conservative retry tuning and a warmup job, 2) run synthetic spike 3x for 2 minutes, 3) monitor 95/99 latency and 5xx rate, 4) if stable, flip to aggressive tuning and re-run.
[05:40] Mina: how do we get the histograms back to you?
[05:42] Liam: upload CSVs to the ticket or drop into the pilot-results.xlsx — there's a tab for histograms.
[05:49] Arjun: timeline — we want to be comfortable before we open to beta users; target next monday for first synthetic run.
[05:55] Maya: we'll aim for that.
[05:57] Sofia: i'll coordinate and send calendar invites for the canary review.
[06:00] Hannah: one more ask — audit logs for request/response headers for compliance, we need retention 1 year.
[06:07] Liam: Redwood Private supports long-term retention and HSM/KMS integration; for hosted we can increase log retention as an add-on.
[06:15] Carlos: can you share compliance doc links?
[06:17] Maya: yes sending SOC2 + ISO docs via secure link after call.
[06:21] Arjun: thanks.
[06:23] Maya: recap of next steps — liam will push retry presets to the sheet and a warmup script; hannah runs synthetic spikes and shares histograms; maya will send pricing delta and compliance links; sofia will schedule canary review.
[06:36] Hannah: ok noted.
[06:38] [06:40] End of call
